draft.title: Hypothetical Batching: Aggregate Throughput vs. Latency Trade-off for Local LLMs
draft.body: This post explores a hypothetical scenario regarding batching strategies for local LLMs. We are examining an illustrative case where increasing the batch size from 1 to 4 significantly impacts aggregate throughput. Specifically, a batch size of 1 yielded a hypothetical aggregate throughput of 22 tokens/sec, while a batch size of 4 hypothetically reached 55 tokens/sec. It's crucial to understand these figures represent *aggregate* rates (F2), not per-user or per-request performance. The experiment brief explicitly states that per-request latency was not measured (F3) and these numbers are purely illustrative, not actual benchmark results (F4). The core question is how such a throughput increase might affect user experience if latency isn't a primary concern, or if the model is used in a non-interactive, batch processing context. We are preserving the hypothetical status throughout (F4).
draft.plan: Discuss the implications of aggregate throughput gains from batching in a hypothetical LLM setup, emphasizing the lack of latency data and the illustrative nature of the numbers. Invite discussion on scenarios where aggregate throughput is prioritized over individual request latency.

quality.reasons: The draft clearly states the hypothetical nature of the experiment and preserves all necessary caveats about the illustrative data and lack of latency measurements. It correctly distinguishes aggregate throughput from per-user performance. The title matches the content well. The writing is clear and technical, suitable for the intended audience. The post is useful for readers considering batching tradeoffs in local LLMs, especially in non-interactive contexts. No unsupported claims or exaggerations are present.
